dedupe_keys.name: nlr evi inmotion design optimisation and feasibility of dynamic in motion ev charging on road networks

description: EVI-InMotion (Electric Vehicle Infrastructure - In Motion) is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) tool for planning, optimising and assessing the feasibility of charging EVs while they drive, for light-, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and inductive, capacitive or conductive technologies. Contents: using high-resolution travel data and road network information, it optimises charger coverage, power, location and length at each location together with onboard battery size and number of power receivers, minimising charger and vehicle component costs while meeting range and charging-time requirements. It combines a vehicle powertrain model (integrated with FASTSim), a cost model, a dynamic inductive charger power model, an automatic placement algorithm built on existing US road networks and a single- or multi-objective search algorithm; versions exist for fixed routes and for public roads. Producer: NLR Transportation and Mobility Research, part of EVI-X. Coverage: US road networks at city or state scale. Format and access: NLR tool; the page gives no public download. Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: component costs and technology parameters are assumptions that change quickly for an emerging technology. Simulation uses: siting electrified road segments, comparing in-motion with stationary charging, and estimating the location and timing of grid loads. Related records: platform-nlr-evi-x-ev-charging-infrastructure-modelling-suite.
